經氣孔進行的蒸騰

1 水份從葉肉細胞表面蒸發，並進入氣室中。

2 氣室內的水汽經氣孔擴散到大氣中。

蒸騰拉力的形成

1 水份從葉肉細胞散失，細胞的水勢因而下降。

2 葉肉細胞藉滲透從鄰近細胞吸收水份。

3 木質導管內的水被抽出，形成蒸騰拉力。

蒸騰是植物體內的水份蒸發，並以水汽形式散失到大氣的過程。水汽主要經葉和草本莖上的氣孔散失。
水份從葉肉細胞表面的水膜蒸發成水汽，進入海綿葉肉中的氣室。當氣室的水汽濃度高於外界大氣，水汽便經氣孔藉擴散離開葉。
葉肉細胞散失水份後，水勢下降，並藉滲透從鄰近細胞吸收水份。水份因而從葉的木質導管被抽出，產生蒸騰拉力，把水份沿莖的木質導管向上牽引。
在水份供應充足等合適條件下，較高的光強度通常使氣孔張得更大，水汽藉擴散離開葉的速率加快，蒸騰速率因而上升。
注意：增加光照亦可能使葉的溫度上升，進一步加快蒸騰。因此，此探究假設所有裝置的溫度相同，以便比較光強度的影響。
蒸騰拉力促使根持續吸收水份，並驅使水份和根吸收的已溶解礦物質沿木質導管向上轉運到葉。

參照課本第 11.1 節，頁 11-3 至 11-8。紅色水跡顯示水分運輸的線索，不能直接等同蒸騰速率；帶葉／不帶葉比較亦不能單獨證明氣孔的作用。

分清兩個過程與植物部位

水分運輸是液態水沿木質部移動；蒸騰是植物失水至大氣的過程。紅色水跡標示液態水運輸的線索，不直接量度散失的水汽。西芹長柄是含木質部的葉柄，並非莖。

假說與公平比較示例

可測試假說指出主動改變的因素及可量度的結果。例如：「其他條件相同，葉面積較大的西芹，紅色水跡平均上移速度較快。」比較兩種葉面積，保持光照等相同，以 cm/min 量度；結果也可能不支持假說。

獨立變量：主動改變的因素；因變量：量度的結果；控制變量：保持相同的因素。公平比較只改變要研究的因素。例如比較葉面積時，保持光照、溫度及量度時間相同。

經氣孔進行的蒸騰

1 水份從葉肉細胞表面蒸發，並進入氣室中。

2 氣室內的水汽經氣孔擴散到大氣中。

蒸騰拉力的形成

1 水份從葉肉細胞散失，細胞的水勢因而下降。

2 葉肉細胞藉滲透從鄰近細胞吸收水份。

3 木質導管內的水被抽出，形成蒸騰拉力。

蒸騰是植物體內的水份蒸發，並以水汽形式散失到大氣的過程。水汽主要經葉和草本莖上的氣孔散失。
水份從葉肉細胞表面的水膜蒸發成水汽，進入海綿葉肉中的氣室。當氣室的水汽濃度高於外界大氣，水汽便經氣孔藉擴散離開葉。
葉肉細胞散失水份後，水勢下降，並藉滲透從鄰近細胞吸收水份。水份因而從葉的木質導管被抽出，產生蒸騰拉力，把水份沿莖的木質導管向上牽引。
在水份供應充足等合適條件下，較高的光強度通常使氣孔張得更大，水汽藉擴散離開葉的速率加快，蒸騰速率因而上升。
注意：增加光照亦可能使葉的溫度上升，進一步加快蒸騰。因此，此探究假設所有裝置的溫度相同，以便比較光強度的影響。
蒸騰拉力促使根持續吸收水份，並驅使水份和根吸收的已溶解礦物質沿木質導管向上轉運到葉。

參照課本第 11.1 節，頁 11-3 至 11-8。紅色水跡顯示水分運輸的線索，不能直接等同蒸騰速率；帶葉／不帶葉比較亦不能單獨證明氣孔的作用。

水分運輸是液態水沿木質部移動；蒸騰是植物失水至大氣的過程。紅色水跡標示液態水運輸的線索，不直接量度散失的水汽。西芹長柄是含木質部的葉柄，並非莖。

Transpiration (蒸騰) is the process in which water in a plant evaporates (蒸發) and is lost to the air as water vapour (水汽). Water vapour (水汽) mainly leaves through stomata (氣孔) in leaves and herbaceous stems (草本莖).
Water evaporates (蒸發) from the water film (水膜) on the surface of mesophyll cells (葉肉細胞) and enters the air spaces (氣室) in the spongy mesophyll as water vapour (水汽). When the water vapour (水汽) concentration in the air spaces (氣室) is higher than in the air outside, water vapour (水汽) leaves the leaf through stomata (氣孔) by diffusion.
When mesophyll cells (葉肉細胞) lose water, their water potential falls. They take in water from nearby cells by osmosis. This draws water out of the leaf's xylem vessels (木質導管) and creates transpiration pull (蒸騰拉力), which pulls water upwards through the stem's xylem vessels (木質導管).
Under suitable conditions, such as enough water being available, higher light intensity (光強度) usually makes stomata (氣孔) open wider. Water vapour (水汽) then leaves the leaf faster by diffusion, so the transpiration rate (蒸騰速率) increases.
Note: More light may also make the leaf's temperature rise, increasing transpiration (蒸騰) further. This investigation therefore assumes that all setups have the same temperature so we can compare the effect of light intensity (光強度).
Transpiration pull (蒸騰拉力) keeps roots taking in water and moves water and dissolved minerals absorbed by the roots upwards through xylem vessels (木質導管) to the leaves.

See textbook section 11.1, pages 11-3 to 11-8. The red water trace gives evidence of water transport. Its upward speed is not a direct measure of the transpiration rate (蒸騰速率). Comparing celery with and without leaves alone also cannot prove the role of stomata (氣孔).

Distinguish processes and plant parts

Water transport is liquid water moving through xylem (木質部). Transpiration (蒸騰) is water loss from a plant to the air. The trace gives evidence of liquid water transport, not a direct measurement of water vapour (水汽) lost. The long celery stalk is a petiole (葉柄) containing xylem (木質部), not a stem.

Hypothesis and fair-comparison example

A testable (可測試的) hypothesis states the factor changed on purpose and a measurable result. Example: “With other conditions the same, celery with a larger leaf area has a faster average upward speed of the red trace.” Compare two leaf areas, keep light and other conditions the same, and measure in cm/min. Results may not support the hypothesis.

Independent variable: the factor changed on purpose. Dependent variable: the measured result. Controlled variables: factors kept the same. A fair comparison changes only the factor being studied. When comparing leaf area, keep light, temperature and measurement time the same.

How transpiration pull (蒸騰拉力) forms

Transpiration (蒸騰) is the process in which water in a plant evaporates (蒸發) and is lost to the air as water vapour (水汽). Water vapour (水汽) mainly leaves through stomata (氣孔) in leaves and herbaceous stems (草本莖).
Water evaporates (蒸發) from the water film (水膜) on the surface of mesophyll cells (葉肉細胞) and enters the air spaces (氣室) in the spongy mesophyll as water vapour (水汽). When the water vapour (水汽) concentration in the air spaces (氣室) is higher than in the air outside, water vapour (水汽) leaves the leaf through stomata (氣孔) by diffusion.
When mesophyll cells (葉肉細胞) lose water, their water potential falls. They take in water from nearby cells by osmosis. This draws water out of the leaf's xylem vessels (木質導管) and creates transpiration pull (蒸騰拉力), which pulls water upwards through the stem's xylem vessels (木質導管).
Under suitable conditions, such as enough water being available, higher light intensity (光強度) usually makes stomata (氣孔) open wider. Water vapour (水汽) then leaves the leaf faster by diffusion, so the transpiration rate (蒸騰速率) increases.
Note: More light may also make the leaf's temperature rise, increasing transpiration (蒸騰) further. This investigation therefore assumes that all setups have the same temperature so we can compare the effect of light intensity (光強度).
Transpiration pull (蒸騰拉力) keeps roots taking in water and moves water and dissolved minerals absorbed by the roots upwards through xylem vessels (木質導管) to the leaves.

Distinguish processes and plant parts

Water transport is liquid water moving through xylem (木質部). Transpiration (蒸騰) is water loss from a plant to the air. The trace gives evidence of liquid water transport, not a direct measurement of water vapour (水汽) lost. The long celery stalk is a petiole (葉柄) containing xylem (木質部), not a stem.

Hypothesis and fair-comparison example

A testable (可測試的) hypothesis states the factor changed on purpose and a measurable result. Example: “With other conditions the same, celery with a larger leaf area has a faster average upward speed of the red trace.” Compare two leaf areas, keep light and other conditions the same, and measure in cm/min. Results may not support the hypothesis.

Independent variable: the factor changed on purpose. Dependent variable: the measured result. Controlled variables: factors kept the same. A fair comparison changes only the factor being studied. When comparing leaf area, keep light, temperature and measurement time the same.

Explanation reference (try your own explanation first):

With suitable conditions and enough water, stronger light usually promotes stomatal opening (氣孔張開) and transpiration (蒸騰). Water evaporates (蒸發) from mesophyll surfaces; vapour diffuses through stomata (氣孔). Water potential falls, water is replaced by osmosis and pulled from xylem (木質部), forming transpiration pull (蒸騰拉力). Data support a transport trend, not a direct transpiration rate (蒸騰速率).
